title: verity.town
description: A 140-account fediverse server for Verity County, run off a kitchen table in Ashkettle on a $9 box, where the content warnings get used properly and almost nothing leaves the building.

profile.bio:
I run this. That is the whole of the staff page.

verity.town is a small server for Verity County. 140 accounts. Fifty-one of them posted last month. I do the office at [url=synth://attwaterexcavating.synth/]Attwater Excavating[/url] and I am not a sysadmin, I am a person who reads changelogs on a Sunday.

[b]Rules[/b]
[list][*]Be a person here. No selling, no growth, no engagement bait.[*]Content warnings on: medical, death, food, drink, politics that is about people rather than about culverts, and anything that flashes.[*]Bots need a flag and an owner who answers mail.[*]No unbroken crossposting from somewhere else. One post a day off a feed is a feed. Nine is a firehose.[*]If you are reported I read the report and I answer you. It takes a day. Sometimes three.[/list]

[b]What it costs[/b]
$9 a month for the box, $3 a month for the volume I added in August, $28 a year for the name. $14.33 a month, and I count the name. Tips cover about 40% of that, which is the highest it has been: [url=/post/p07]the September post[/url]. Please do not feel anything about this.

[b]What it does not do[/b]
No algorithm. No quote posts. No full-text search past 30 days. No analytics — I could not tell you which post did best this week, and neither could anybody else here, and that is not a bug I am going to fix.

Block list, with reasons: [url=/post/p17]here[/url]. Migration notes from March 2025: [url=/post/p01]here[/url], still unread by most of you.

Abuse contact is this account. Not a form.

feed.author: Rosalind Brumm
feed.body:
[b]Pinned.[/b] Read this before you ask me where your direct messages went.

We are off Parlance as of about four o'clock this afternoon. They went from $6 a month to $29 a month on 1 February in a blog post I did not see, and I am not paying $348 a year for 140 people who mostly post about weather.

[b]What moved[/b]
[list][*]Your account, your posts, your followers, your follows, your lists.[*]Your uploads, most of them. Anything posted before March 2023 lost its file and kept its post. You will see a grey box. That is the box.[/list]

[b]What did not move[/b]
[list][*]Direct messages. All of them. Gone, on both ends, permanently. I said this four times in February and I am saying it a fifth time here.[*]Saved drafts.[*]Scheduled posts, which is why three of you posted nothing for a week and thought you had been quietly throttled.[/list]

[b]What you have to do[/b]
Nothing, if you logged in today and it worked. If a client asks you to sign in again, sign in again. The address is the same address — that was the point of paying for the name in 2022.

Backups run at 3am and I keep fourteen of them. Your own export is in Settings and I would rather you had one than trusted me.

— Roz

feed.author: Rosalind Brumm
feed.body:
cw: none, this is server housekeeping and it is dull

The box has a 60 GB disk and 51 GB of it was other people's avatars.

Remote media — every image, every header, every custom emoji from every server anybody here follows — was set to cache for 90 days, because 90 days is the default and I never changed it. It is 14 days now.

Numbers, because I said I would always give you the numbers:
[list][*]Before: 51.4 GB of cached remote media, 6.2 GB of ours.[*]After the prune: 7.8 GB of cached remote media, 6.2 GB of ours.[*]Time: 41 minutes, nearly all of it the delete.[/list]

What you will see: images on old posts from other servers go grey until somebody opens the post and it fetches them again. If the other server is gone, it stays grey forever. Two of the servers in our timeline history are gone.

Our own uploads are untouched and stay untouched. I added a $3 volume in August so I would stop having to think about this, and then I thought about it anyway.

If the disk ever does fill, the thing that breaks first is not posting. It is the database. And then I am restoring from a 3am backup like an idiot. So: 14 days.

feed.author: Tamsin Boesch
feed.body:
cw: night driving, and the thing on 62, which I know some of you are tired of

I do the Ashkettle to Halsey run three nights a week and I keep a radio in the truck because the phone gets nothing past the cut.

11:07 last night. 4.2190. The voice, four digits at a time, same as it has been every odd hour since before I could drive. I do not have a theory about it. I have a thermos.

What I actually wanted to say is that there were six cars in the pull-off at the quarry cut. Six. A Friday in September. Two people were standing on car roofs holding phones up.

There is no shoulder there. The sheriff's office has said there is no law against parking on the 62 shoulder, which is true, and which is not the same as it being a good idea, and one of those six was half in the lane.

[url=synth://milbrookgazette.com/article/shoulder-parking]The Gazette wrote that up in 2016[/url]. Same pull-off. Same argument. Ten years of the same argument and now there are six cars in it.

The tip page, since three people have asked and one person has asked twice.

It exists. It has been up since April. It is not in the sidebar and it is not going in the sidebar.

September so far: $6.00, from four people. The bill is $14.33. So it covers about 40%, which is the highest it has ever been, and I wanted it written down somewhere before it goes back to 20% in October.

Two of the four give a dollar. I am telling you that on purpose. On a server this size a dollar is not a token, it is seven percent of the electricity bill for the county's only room where nobody is selling anything.

What I will not do with it:
[list][*]Turn it into a membership.[*]Put a badge on anybody.[*]Put a bar at the top of the page that fills up.[/list]

What happens if it stops: nothing. The $14.33 comes out of the same account as the propane and it has since 2022.

If you have money for something in the county this month, put it in [url=/post/p05]Marta's pantry[/url] instead. They need a Thursday driver more than they need the money, and they need the money more than I need $1.50.

cw: the federation thing again, sorry, and then I will stop

I am going to raise it one more time.

openfield.social has about 96,000 accounts. We have 140. My sister lives in Halsey, eleven miles from me, and she cannot see anything I write unless she goes looking for it, because we do not federate with them and their relay is the one everybody else in this state is on.

The reasons we said no in June were: their reports go to a contractor, their block list is shorter than ours, and Roz would be doing moderation for 96,000 people's worth of replies to 140 people's posts.

Those are all still true. I am asking whether they are worth what we pay for them, which is that this place is quiet.

[url=/post/p22]The June thread is here.[/url] I have read it again this evening. I have not changed my mind, and I am aware that makes me the tedious one.

feed.author: Anneliese Krug
feed.body:
cw: local politics, school buses, long

Kerrin consolidated is losing two bus routes in January and the board spent four minutes on it.

What is happening: routes 4 and 7 merge. The merged route is 71 minutes end to end. There are six-year-olds at the far end of route 7.

What was said at the meeting: that the merge is driver availability, which is true, and that it is temporary, which is also what was said in 2023 about the route they merged in 2023.

What was not said: that the district has been two drivers short since March, and advertised the job once, on [url=synth://verity-careers-portal.com/]the county careers portal[/url], at $18.40 an hour. The highway department pays more than that to plough.

I am not neutral here. I teach fourth grade and four of mine are on route 7. But the four minutes is the thing I keep coming back to. They spent forty on the dress code.

The Gazette ran a story in 2016 with exactly that shape. Four minutes on the bus, forty on the dress code. [url=synth://milbrookgazette.com/article/board-oct]Here it is.[/url]

The paper stopped that same October. The meetings did not.

feed.author: Reg Cavey
feed.body:
cw: scan, four pages, and a small complaint at the end

The Kestrel Letter came Saturday. Autumn issue. Four pages, photocopied, staple in the top left at the same angle it has been at for years.

[img:photo:kestrel-letter-autumn-2026]

Page two is the booth by the window and who sat in it on Sunday mornings between 1974 and 1977, with names, and where they parked. Page three is the pie recipe again, with a line added at the bottom saying it was never a good pie and she has stopped apologising for it.

I scan it because sixty-one people get it in the post and three of those are libraries. Her own site has been sitting there unchanged since 2019 — [url=synth://kestrel-journal.net/]it is still up[/url], and she has said she is not going back to it.

The complaint: this scan has now been labelled [b]Synthetic media — likely AI-generated[/b] by the thing attached to this server. A photocopy of a typed newsletter, made by a woman in Coyne Flats who does not use the internet, on purpose.

feed.author: Ife Okonkwo
feed.body:
cw: medical, hospital pharmacy, nothing bad happens to anybody

We changed ordering systems at County General in June. Third system since I started in 2019.

It is better in one way, and I want to say that first: it flags two interactions the old one missed. That is not nothing. That is the whole reason to have a system.

It is worse in four ways, and all four are the same way, which is that it was built for a hospital with a pharmacy that is open twenty-four hours. Ours is not.

Between eleven at night and seven in the morning it will let a floor order something we cannot dispense until morning, and it does not say so. It says pending. It has said pending for eight hours and then gone on saying pending.

We have a workaround. The workaround is a laminated sheet taped to the counter with a phone number on it.

Every system I have ever worked with ends as a laminated sheet. Nobody has been harmed and I want to be clear about that. But the sheet is the actual interface, and not one person who bought that software has ever seen the sheet.

replies.body: Every system I have ever worked with ends as a laminated sheet. I am going to be thinking about that all week and probably at work.

Shut all day Thursday 10 September. Parts run, and the machine that does screens is being serviced.

Walk-in again Friday from nine. If you left a phone with us Monday it is finished and you can collect it Friday.

Batteries for the 2019 to 2022 models are back in. No appointment, we have never taken appointments, please stop ringing to make one.

We are in the old Blue Kestrel building on 62. The bird on the roof is not ours and is staying. The lit sign underneath it is ours. [url=synth://carrowwireless.com/hours]Hours are on the site[/url] and they are correct, which took some doing.

feed.author: Rosalind Brumm
feed.body:
The block list, updated, with reasons. I publish it because a server that blocks quietly is a server you cannot check.

[b]Suspended[/b] — nothing passes, either direction
[list][*]brightside.host — 900 accounts, all of them feeds, one contact address and it bounces.[*]freeforall.zone — open registration, no moderation policy of any kind, 31 reports from here in June alone.[*]copperkettle.social — one user. Nine months. I asked their admin twice.[*]newsdeck.bot — a syndication farm. Every post is a headline and a link and there are about four thousand a day.[*]county-energy-credit.win — the rebate one. Registered in July, suspended here in July, and it will be back under a different name.[/list]

[b]Limited[/b] — you can follow them, they do not appear in the public timeline
[list][*]pondsight.social — mostly fine. One prolific user who is not.[*]allcounty.news — a local-news network. Four hundred towns, one template, no staff. We are one of the four hundred.[/list]

[b]Not blocked, and asked about every month[/b]
[list][*]openfield.social — we do not federate with them, which is not the same as blocking them, and I am tired of the two being run together.[*]gridline.social — not a fediverse server at all. You cannot block it from here. You can stop mirroring it into here, which is a different conversation and we have had it.[/list]

Appeals come to me. I have reversed exactly one block in three years and I will tell you which if you ask: copperkettle, in 2024. I put it back in January.

replies.author: Wendell Sipes
replies.body: Thank you for the not-blocked section. Every other server's list leaves that out and then people assume, and then the assumption is what gets repeated.

replies.author: Rosalind Brumm
replies.body: It is the one that runs real obituaries with the town name swapped. Which I think is worse, and which is why it is limited and not suspended, because people's relatives are in there and somebody might want to find one.

replies.author: Del Meeker
replies.body: Limited rather than suspended is the right call and it is the harder one. Suspending is easy. Suspending feels like doing something.

replies.author: Rosalind Brumm
replies.body: It is nine months of evenings written down as eleven words. That is what a block list is. Eleven words per year of somebody's life.

feed.author: Dov Lurie
feed.body:
cw: a goodbye, and not a dramatic one

I have moved my main account to openfield.social. Not because of anything. Nobody did anything.

I drive for the transit authority and I am on a phone for eleven hours a day and I want the app that works on a phone. Theirs does. The one I can use here does not, and Roz cannot fix that, because it is not hers to fix and never was.

I am leaving this account up and forwarding it. Everything I have posted here stays here. I am not deleting five years because I changed apps.

Things I will miss, specifically:
[list][*]Knowing who everybody is without having to check.[*]Marta's numbers on the first week of the month.[*]That when somebody here is wrong, one person says so, once, and then it is over.[/list]

Things I will not miss: nothing. There is nothing.

I will still be reading. My replies will arrive from a different address and you will all be able to tell, which I find funny and which will stop being funny in about a week.

feed.author: North Relay
feed.body:
VERITY COUNTY: Rail Trail Named Among Region's Best

The Verity Branch Trail, a 14-mile crushed stone path built on the former Verity Rail branch line which closed in 2009, has been named one of the region's best rail trails.

Residents say the trail is a popular destination for walking and cycling. Local officials have described the trail as an asset to the community.

The route crosses four historic trestles, all of which are open to pedestrians and offer scenic views of the surrounding countryside.

Visitors to {{town_name}} are encouraged to plan their visit in advance.

[url=synth://now.verityledger.com/article/a-04]Read more[/url]

feed.author: Del Meeker
feed.body:
cw: long, and it is the newspaper thing again

Ten years this October since the Milbrook Gazette printed anything. The note to readers said the pause was temporary and blamed a printer contract. [url=synth://milbrookgazette.com/article/note-to-readers]It is still sitting on the site[/url], which is still up, and that is the part that gets me.

Since then the north end has had nothing. I do not mean nothing good. I mean the village board has met the first Tuesday of every month for ten years and there is no written record of what happened at any of them except the minutes, and the minutes are not a record of what happened. They are a record of what was voted on.

Two things that happened up here this year that nobody outside the room knows:
[list][*]The Cobb Creek bridge posting went from eight tons to six in May. Two bus routes changed again. The Gazette covered the eight-ton posting in 2016 and there is nobody to cover the six.[*]The Tessler post office window went to two hours a day. It was four. The Gazette covered the four.[/list]

I read [url=synth://thequarry.news/i/i-78]The Quarry[/url] and I read [url=synth://brenners-notebook.email/i/i-77]Brenner's thing[/url], and between them that is two people covering a county, and they are both down the south end, and that is not a criticism. That is arithmetic.

feed.author: Rosalind Brumm
feed.body:
Asking properly, once: do we want to federate with openfield.social.

What it would get us: about 96,000 accounts of reach, the relay most of the state is already on, and your posts being visible to people you actually know who happen to be over there.

What it would cost:
[list][*]Reports. I get four or five a week and they are local and nearly all of them are spam. Servers our size that join a big relay describe going to forty or fifty, and the new ones are arguments between strangers about things that did not happen here.[*]The public timeline. Ours is readable top to bottom in an evening. That is not a design achievement. That is 140 people.[*]Me. One person, a laptop, a kitchen table, and I have been honest with you about that since 2022.[/list]

I am not asking you to vote. I am asking what you think, and then I will decide, because it is my name on the abuse contact, and that is how this actually works whatever anybody says about it.

Say your piece. I will read all of it.
